separate_source_refutations.claim: pytest.ini timeout=600 is inert because pytest-timeout is not installed
separate_source_refutations.source_text:
code/pytest.ini — pytest.ini declares timeout = 600 but pytest-timeout is installed nowhere.

The premise (pytest-timeout absent from CI install list and requirements_latest.txt) is true, but the conclusion is wrong: code/conftest.py implements its own timeout support. Line 16 sets PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 (external plugins deliberately blocked), line 108 registers the 'timeout' ini option via parser.addini (so it is NOT an unknown-option warning), pytest_configure line 93 parses it, and the pytest_runtest_call hookwrapper (lines 117-133) arms signal.alarm(600) per test and raises TimeoutError on expiry. The comment at line 82 says explicitly 'Simple built-in timeout support (pytest-timeout is disabled by plugin block)'. The per-test 600s timeout therefore IS enforced on the ubuntu CI runner and local macOS (SIGALRM available); a hung test gets a per-test TimeoutError, not a silent 30-minute job kill. Residual truth: no effect on Windows and no coverage for hangs outside the main-thread test call, but the finding's core claim ('silently inert everywhere') is false.
